# Quantum Aether — post-quantum TLS readiness scanner

> Checks whether an HTTPS server negotiates the hybrid post-quantum key exchange X25519MLKEM768 (ML-KEM, FIPS 203) used by Chrome and Firefox, and reports TLS version and certificate details. Free summary; full report with remediation steps costs ${{ price }} via PayPal.

## Free API

- `POST {{ base }}/api/scan` with JSON `{"domain": "example.com"}` returns a summary: grade (A/B/C/F), TLS version, negotiated key-exchange group, whether it is post-quantum, certificate key, number of findings. Rate limited per client.
- `GET {{ base }}/api/scan/{scan_id}` returns the same summary later.
- `POST {{ base }}/api/v1/quantum-scan` is the agent endpoint: `{"domain": "example.com"}` runs the same real scan; `{"key_size": 2048}` alone returns an honest assessment of that RSA key size (no network scan). Any RSA or ECC key size is breakable by Shor's algorithm; key exchange is what needs upgrading.
- The full report is paid on the scan page with PayPal; a person approves the payment.
- OpenAPI description: {{ base }}/openapi.yaml

## Grades

- A: TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange.
- B: TLS 1.3 with classical key exchange only (exposed to harvest-now-decrypt-later).
- C: no TLS 1.3.
- F: invalid certificate, legacy TLS, static RSA key exchange or RSA below 2048 bits.

## Research

- {{ base }}/research — a 3-qubit GHZ circuit run on IBM Quantum hardware (ibm_marrakesh) and a research report archived as digital DNA with Reed-Solomon error correction.
